mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which may stimulate economic growth and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day periods following low FEDFUNDS, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A high unemployment rate suggests economic weakness, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of the periods when UNRATE exceeds 9%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Strong retail sales indicate positive consumer sentiment and economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If retail sales growth is accompanied by negative S&P returns in more than 30% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Low industrial production may signal supply chain issues or reduced economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If industrial production is low but S&P returns are positive in more than 40% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Strong employment numbers indicate a robust labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If employment growth does not correlate with positive S&P returns (correlation < 0.2), the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment combined with falling employment suggests economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by 0.5% and PAYEMS decreases
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 30% of cases with rising UNRATE and falling PAYEMS, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: High housing starts indicate strong demand in the housing market, which may lead to positive economic growth and S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If housing starts are high but S&P returns are negative in more than 40% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth combined with high inflation may lead to negative S&P 500 returns as higher interest rates could reduce corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 35% of cases with high GDP and inflation, the hypothesis is rejected.
